ai.literal: The battle-axe of desire will break the door called self-control, which is fastened by the bolt of shyness.
ai.translation: The battle-axe of desire will break open the door of my self-control, which is secured by the bolt of modesty.
ai.modern: நாணம் என்னும் தாழ்ப்பாள் போடப்பட்ட நிறை (மனக்கட்டுப்பாடு) என்னும் கதவை, காமம் என்னும் கோடரி உடைத்துவிடும்.
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the speaker describes how overwhelming love-passion overpowers their reserve. The poet employs a vivid metaphor of a house: the mind's self-control (niraiv) is a protective door, and modesty (nāṇ) is the strong bolt securing it. However, the intense desire (kāmam) acts as a sharp battle-axe (kaṇicci) that easily shatters this bolted door, exposing the hidden feelings. This illustrates the helplessness of a lover when passion exceeds the limits of modesty.

ai.literal: Passion called one thing, compassion without, my heart, even at midnight, ruling task.
ai.translation: This thing called passion has no compassion; its only task is to rule over my heart even at the dead of night.
ai.modern: காமம் என்று சொல்லப்படும் ஒன்று இரக்கமே இல்லாமல், நள்ளிரவிலும் என் நெஞ்சத்தை ஆளுகின்ற தொழிலைச் செய்கிறது.
ai.explanation: The heroine laments her helplessness against her overwhelming desire. She describes passion (காமம்) as a merciless entity that lacks 'கண்' (which here means regard or compassion) for her suffering. Even during 'யாமம்' (midnight), when the rest of the world is asleep and she ought to rest, passion continues its relentless task ('தொழில்') of dominating her mind ('நெஞ்சத்தை').

ai.literal: I will indeed hide my love, I? Without warning, like a sneeze, appearing it will escape.
ai.translation: I try indeed to hide my love, but like a sneeze, it bursts forth suddenly without warning.
ai.modern: நான் என் காமத்தை மறைக்கவே நினைக்கிறேன்; ஆனால் அது, ஒரு தும்மலைப் போல, எந்தவித முன்னறிவிப்பும் இல்லாமல் திடீரென்று வெளிப்பட்டு விடுகிறது.
ai.explanation: The heroine laments her inability to conceal her intense love-sickness. She asserts that she tries her best to hide her feelings ('மறைப்பேன்'). However, love is not something that can be suppressed by willpower. It is compared to a sneeze ('தும்மல்'), which cannot be stopped or anticipated; it bursts out suddenly without warning ('குறிப்பின்றி'). Just as a sneeze reveals itself despite one's efforts to hold it back, her love reveals itself to others, rendering her attempts at secrecy futile.

ai.literal: Self-control possessor I would say indeed, as for me; my love, secret transgressing, in the public place will appear.
ai.translation: I used to boast that I possessed self-control; but my love, breaking past all secrecy, now stands revealed in the public square.
ai.modern: நான் மனக்கட்டுப்பாடு உடையவள் என்றுதான் சொல்லிக்கொண்டிருந்தேன்; ஆனால் என் காமமானது இரகசியத்தைக் கடந்து பொதுவெளியில் வெளிப்பட்டு நிற்கிறது.
ai.explanation: The heroine laments her inability to conceal her intense love-sickness. She recalls how she once believed she had the strength and self-control (niṟai) to keep her feelings hidden. However, her passion (kāmam) has grown so powerful that it has broken through all boundaries of secrecy (maṟai) and is now visible to everyone in the public square (maṉṟu). The particle 'maṉ' highlights her past confidence, which has now turned into helpless exposure.

words.gloss: those who have disliked or abandoned us

ai.literal: The great dignity of not going after those who disliked us is not one thing known by those who suffer from the disease of love.
ai.translation: The noble dignity of not running after those who have abandoned us is not something known to those who suffer from the affliction of love.
ai.modern: நம்மை வெறுத்து நீங்கியவர் பின்னே செல்லாமல் இருக்கும் பெருந்தன்மை, காமநோயால் வருந்துபவர்கள் அறியக்கூடிய ஒன்று அல்ல.
ai.explanation: This couplet describes the loss of self-control and dignity under the influence of intense love. Normally, self-respect demands that one should not pursue someone who has shown dislike or abandoned them. However, the speaker confesses that such noble restraint is impossible for those afflicted with the disease of love. Their overwhelming passion breaks all barriers of pride, forcing them to seek out the very person who caused them pain.

ai.literal: Desiring to go behind him who was angry, pitiable indeed! Of what nature is the sorrow that has befallen me!
ai.translation: Desiring to follow after the one who showed anger, how pitiable indeed is my state! What kind of strange grief is this that has come upon me?
ai.modern: என்னிடம் கோபித்துக் கொண்டு சென்ற காதலரின் பின்னே போக விரும்புவதால், எனக்கு நேர்ந்த இந்தத் துன்பம் மிகவும் இரங்கத்தக்கது; இது என்ன வகையான துன்பமோ!
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the heroine laments her complete loss of reserve and self-control. Although her lover has behaved coldly or departed in anger, her heart still desperately desires to follow him. She finds her own helpless state highly pitiable, as indicated by the words 'அளித்து அரோ'. She wonders what kind of strange, overwhelming grief ('எற்று என்னை உற்ற துயர்') has taken hold of her, forcing her to abandon her dignity and run after someone who showed her hostility.

ai.literal: Modesty called one thing we do not know, if by love those who cherished (us) do pleasing things.
ai.translation: We know nothing of a thing called modesty, if our beloved, out of love, acts in ways that please us.
ai.modern: நம்மை விரும்பிய காதலர், காதலினால் நமக்கு விருப்பமானவற்றைச் செய்யும்போது, நாணம் என்று சொல்லப்படும் ஒரு குணத்தை நாம் அறியமாட்டோம்.
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the heroine describes how her natural reserve and modesty completely dissolve in the warmth of her lover's affection. She states that when her beloved, whom she deeply cherishes, acts out of love to do things that please her, she loses all awareness of what is called modesty ('நாண்'). The word 'பெட்ப' refers to pleasing or desirable actions that bring joy. The verse highlights how the overwhelming power of mutual love ('காமம்') naturally overcomes any sense of restraint or hesitation.

ai.literal: The many-deceitful thief's humble words, are they not the weapon that breaks our feminine reserve?
ai.translation: Are not the submissive words of that thief of many deceits the very weapon that shatters our feminine reserve?
ai.modern: பல ஏமாற்று வேலைகளைச் செய்யும் கள்வனாகிய காதலனின் பணிவான சொற்கள் அல்லவா நம்முடைய பெண்மைத் தன்மையை உடைக்கும் கருவியாக இருக்கின்றன!
ai.explanation: The heroine speaks of her lover, whom she calls a thief of many deceits because he easily steals her heart despite her resolve. She realizes that her feminine reserve and self-control are completely shattered not by force, but by his gentle, submissive, and humble words. These soft words act as a powerful weapon that breaks down her defenses. The couplet beautifully contrasts the strength of a weapon with the softness of humble speech, showing how tenderness can conquer firm resolve.

ai.literal: 'I will feign anger,' saying to myself I went; I embraced him, seeing my heart desiring to unite.
ai.translation: I went with the resolve to feign anger, but I ended up embracing him, seeing my own heart rushing to unite with him.
ai.modern: நான் அவனிடம் ஊடல் கொள்ள வேண்டும் என்று நினைத்துச் சென்றேன்; ஆனால் என் நெஞ்சம் அவனுடன் கூடுவதற்கு விரைவதைக் கண்டு, அவனைத் தழுவிக்கொண்டேன்.
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the heroine describes how her resolve to remain angry melts away in her lover's presence. She approaches him intending to feign anger ('புலப்பல்') to test his love. However, upon seeing him, she realizes her own heart ('நெஞ்சம்') is already eager to unite ('கலத்தல் உறுவது') with him. Unable to resist her own heart's desire, she immediately embraces him ('புல்லினேன்'), showing that love triumphs over stubborn pride.

words.gloss: to those who have a heart

ai.literal: Like fat thrown in fire, to those who have such a heart, is there the ability of saying 'having united, we will remain sulking'?
ai.translation: Is it possible for those whose hearts melt like fat thrown into fire to resolve, 'We will remain sulking even after we unite'?
ai.modern: நெருப்பில் போட்ட கொழுப்பு உருகுவது போல உருகும் நெஞ்சத்தை உடையவர்க்கு, 'கூடிப் பின் பிணங்கி நிற்போம்' என்று நினைப்பது முடியுமா?
ai.explanation: This couplet describes the vulnerability of a lover's heart when facing their beloved. The speaker compares their heart to fat thrown into a fire, which melts instantly without resistance. Because of this rapid melting of resolve, it is impossible to maintain a state of feigned anger or sulking after meeting. The imagery of melting fat highlights how love completely dissolves any self-control or determination to stay apart.
